questions.prompt: What does the law of conservation of mass say?
options: Matter is never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction
Matter appears when a reaction runs
Matter always becomes lighter in reactions
questions.explanation: The law says matter is never created or destroyed — it is only rearranged.
questions.misconception: Matter never appears or disappears in any chemical reaction — the atoms always carry through from start to finish.

questions.prompt: A log burns to ash that looks lighter than the log. Where did the mass go?
options: It went into the smoke and gases — the atoms were rearranged, not destroyed
The ash is lighter because atoms shrink
questions.explanation: The log's atoms became ash, smoke, and gases — if you weighed ALL the products, the mass would match.
questions.misconception: Atoms are never destroyed and never shrink — the 'missing' mass simply left as smoke and gases that you did not collect.

questions.prompt: How does the total mass of the products compare to the total mass of the reactants?
questions.explanation: Because the same atoms are present throughout, the product mass equals the reactant mass exactly.
questions.misconception: The mass can never differ — the products are the same atoms rearranged, so the total weight is identical.

questions.prompt: Why must chemical equations be balanced?
options: Because the same atoms must appear on both sides — conservation of mass
questions.explanation: Balancing an equation reflects the law — equal atoms (and therefore equal mass) on both sides.
questions.misconception: Balancing is not decoration — it is a factual requirement. Unbalanced equations would claim atoms appear or vanish, which never happens.
